questions.question: How wide should BUG-280's fix go on LocalBackend?

options.label: Three scans + recursive (Recommended)
options.description: Map PermissionError → PermissionDenied in list_files (all three branches: iterdir, rglob, os.walk), list_folders, iter_children. Recursive walks raise on a denied subtree instead of silently dropping it, matching SFTP. User-visible: a partially unreadable tree now raises mid-iteration where it used to return a short listing. glob's same silent drop gets filed as a follow-up.

options.label: Three scans + recursive + glob
options.description: As above, and glob() also raises PermissionDenied on a denied subtree. Wider behaviour change in one PR; glob's contract for denied subtrees isn't stated in the spec yet, so this also needs a spec sentence.

options.label: Literal item only
options.description: Fix only the non-recursive iterdir scans in the three methods. Smallest diff, but leaves list_files(denied) raising while list_files(denied, recursive=True) returns []: an inconsistency the fix itself creates. Recursive silent drop filed separately.

questions.question: The item's open decision: fix here, or fix the listing-generator pattern once across backends?

options.label: Fix here only (Recommended)
options.description: Patch LocalBackend's listings. S3Boto3 (BUG-249) and SFTP (BUG-146) are already fixed, so Local is the remaining known instance. The 'once across backends' mechanism is RFC-0017's contract kernel, which already cites BUG-280 as motivation. Record that pointer in the close.

options.label: Shared base helper now
options.description: Add a listing-error wrapper in the Backend base and route Local through it. That pre-empts RFC-0017's design in a bug-fix PR, and the existing S3/SFTP fixes would stay as they are anyway.

questions.question: LocalBackend.glob() drops a denied subtree silently. Path.glob's selector wraps scandir in `except OSError: pass`, which is the same shape BUG-280 fixes in recursive list_files. Should it get its own backlog item?

options.label: File a new BUG item (Recommended)
options.description: New BUG-NNN (ID from gen_backlogid), effort S, spec BE-021/GLOB, with a dossier holding this measurement. Listed in the trace's discovery_followups and cited from the BACKLOG-DONE entry for BUG-280.

options.label: Note it in BUG-280 only
options.description: Record the glob gap in BUG-280's BACKLOG-DONE entry as a stated residue, with no new item. Cheaper, but nothing in the open backlog tracks it.
